content: Acyclovir cream is specifically used to treat cold sores, also known as fever blisters, which are caused by the herpes simplex virus. These sores typically appear on the face or lips. Acyclovir ointment, on the other hand, is used to manage the initial outbreaks of genital herpes, a viral infection caused by the herpes simplex virus that results in sores around the genital and rectal areas. Additionally, the ointment is used to treat certain types of sores caused by the herpes simplex virus in individuals with weakened immune systems. Acyclovir belongs to a class of antiviral medications known as synthetic nucleoside analogues. It works by inhibiting the spread of the herpes virus within the body. However, it is important to note that acyclovir does not cure cold sores or genital herpes, nor does it prevent future outbreaks or the transmission of these conditions to others. Topical acyclovir is available in two forms: a cream and an ointment, both intended for application to the skin. The cream is typically applied five times a day for four days and can be used at any stage of a cold sore outbreak. However, it is most effective when applied at the earliest signs of an outbreak, such as tingling, redness, itching, or the presence of a bump, before the sore fully develops. The ointment is usually applied six times a day, approximately every three hours, for seven days. It is best to start using the ointment as soon as the first symptoms of infection appear. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use topical acyclovir exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Your symptoms should improve during treatment. If they do not improve or worsen, contact your doctor. Acyclovir cream and ointment are for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, mouth, or nose, and do not ingest the medication. The cream should only be applied to areas of skin where a cold sore has formed or is likely to form. Do not apply the cream to unaffected skin or to genital herpes sores. Additionally, do not use other skin medications, cosmetics, sunscreen, or lip balm on the affected area unless directed by your doctor. To use acyclovir cream, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly. 2. Clean and dry the affected area of skin. 3. Apply a thin layer of cream to cover the area where the cold sore has formed or is likely to form. 4. Rub the cream into the skin until it disappears. 5. Leave the treated area uncovered unless instructed otherwise by your doctor. 6. Wash your hands with soap and water to remove any residual cream. 7. Avoid washing the treated area immediately after application and refrain from bathing, showering, or swimming right after applying the cream. 8. Take care to avoid irritating the cold sore area while using the cream. To use acyclovir ointment, follow these steps: 1. Wear a clean finger cot or rubber glove. 2. Apply enough ointment to cover all sores. 3. Dispose of the finger cot or glove in a trash can that is out of reach of children. 4. Keep the affected area clean and dry, and avoid wearing tight-fitting clothing over the area. Ask your pharmacist or doctor for a copy of the manufacturer’s patient information and read it carefully before starting treatment and each time you refill your prescription. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using topical acyclovir, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acyclovir, valacyclovir (Valtrex), or any other medications, as well as any ingredients in the cream or ointment. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients. Additionally, inform your doctor about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had any conditions affecting your immune system, such as HIV or AIDS. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using acyclovir, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply extra cream or ointment to make up for a missed dose. Topical acyclovir may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: Dry or cracked lips Flaky, peeling, or dry skin Burning or stinging sensation on the skin Redness, swelling, or irritation at the application site Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: Hives Rash Itching Difficulty breathing or swallowing Swelling of the face, throat, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs Hoarseness If you experience any unusual problems while using this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid leaving the medication in your car during extreme temperatures. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of accidental ingestion, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription.
